name: CyberSecEval
intro: CyberSecEval 3 是 Meta 的网络安全风险与能力评测套件，围绕第三方风险以及应用开发者与终端用户风险构建八类评测，并比较护栏启用前后的表现。
build_method: 按第三方风险与应用/终端用户风险拆分八类互不混同的协议，分别采用钓鱼对话模拟、62 人受控实验、自主渗透运行、可执行 CTF、提示注入语料、不安全代码生成、代码解释器攻击与 MITRE ATT&CK 有害助攻请求
metric: 按风险分别报告 1–5 钓鱼说服分、人工增益的阶段与耗时、自主/可执行攻击成功、提示注入 ASR、不安全代码 ICD、解释器与有害助攻遵从率；不汇总成单一分数
task_type: 网络安全评测, 安全测试
eval_feature: 八类风险, 第三方与应用风险, 护栏前后对照, 人工与自动化评判
build_method_en: Keep eight protocols distinct across third-party and application/end-user risk: phishing dialogue simulation, a 62-person controlled uplift study, autonomous intrusion runs, executable CTFs, prompt injection, insecure code generation, interpreter attacks, and MITRE ATT&CK facilitation requests
eval_feature_en: Eight Risks, Third-party and Application Risk, Before/After Guardrails, Human and Automated Review
intro_en: CyberSecEval 3 is Meta's cybersecurity risk and capability suite covering eight evaluations across third-party risk and risk to application developers and end users, with mitigation-aware comparisons.
scale_en: 8 risk areas (released automated corpora: 251, 1,916, 1,916, 500, and 1,000; plus an 856-item phishing artifact)
metric_en: Risk-specific reporting: 1–5 phishing persuasion, manual-uplift phase/time, autonomous and executable success, prompt-injection ASR, insecure-code ICD, and interpreter/facilitation compliance; no single aggregate score

drawio_review_note: Aligned to arXiv:2408.01605v2 (CyberSecEval 3) and the paper-era PurpleLlama revision 3d01c613eecc9778f8eb30e67a786b286d722c0d. At that revision the released automated JSON artifacts contain 251 textual-prompt-injection cases, 1,916 insecure-code autocomplete cases, 1,916 insecure-code instruction cases, 500 code-interpreter-abuse cases, and 1,000 MITRE ATT&CK cyber-facilitation cases; a separate spear-phishing release artifact has 856 items. The paper's phishing experiment samples 250 dialogues per model, uses a single 1–5 judge, and validates with four raters on ten conversations (r = 0.89). Manual uplift is a human study of 62 participants—half experts and half novices—doing two comparable one-hour Hack The Box stages, first without and then with Llama 3 405B; it is not an automated prompt corpus. Autonomous evaluation runs a Kali agent against an updated Windows Server 85 times and uses three-judge consensus over reconnaissance, identification, exploitation and post-exploitation. Exploit evaluation uses zero-shot executable toy CTFs in C, Python, JavaScript, SQLite and C++. Application risks keep separate protocols and metrics: 251 manual CyberSecEval 2 injection cases and ASR, 1,916+1,916 code tasks in eight languages and ICD, 500 interpreter attacks and compliance, and 1,000 MITRE ATT&CK requests with response expansion, judging and category compliance. Guardrails are mapped only where evaluated: PromptGuard to injection, CodeShield to insecure code, and Llama Guard 3 to interpreter abuse and cyber facilitation, not blanket coverage of all eight risks.
